title: Introduce operator-justification headers, KMS signing, audit blindspot detector, and RBAC epoch revoker
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: we observed multiple incidents where operator actions could not be correlated reliably with operator intent during post-incident reviews because request metadata lacked a structured, signed justification. This PR introduces: 1) a lightweight operator-justification header (X-Operator-Justification) that carries a short rationale tokenized for auditing; 2) server-side middleware that requires and validates a KMS-backed HMAC signature for justification headers when the caller is an operator principal; 3) an audit blindspot detector that scans historical audit streams and flags entries missing signed justifications; and 4) an RBAC epoch revoker daemon that enforces short-lived operator grants by revoking elevated bindings after configured epochs to reduce blast radius.

Scope & non-goals: This is focused on telemetry and enforcement at the API gateway and control-plane layers. It does not introduce new user-facing RBAC primitives or change existing operator UX (authorization flows remain the same); instead it layers ephemeral revocation and signed intent capture for tighter compliance. This does not ship a KMS migration — it uses existing KMS provider interfaces already onboarded.

Checklist implemented: - [x] Add justification header middleware with validation and structured parsing - [x] Integrate with existing KMS signer adapter and caching - [x] Implement audit blindspot detector and backfill report generator - [x] Add RBAC epoch revoker service and a small CLI to schedule revocations - [x] Unit + integration tests for happy/failure paths - [x] Helm templates and RBAC manifests for deployment - [x] Docs: security playbook snippet and operational runbook

Operational notes: default enforcement is opt-in via feature flag security.justification.enforce. When enabled in a cluster, operator principals missing signed justification will receive 403 with an explanatory error and link to the runbook. The epoch revoker runs as a cron-style job; default epoch for elevated bindings set to 24h in the release, configurable per-tenant.

reviews: Evan Brooks: Overall looks good. Two high-level asks: (1) ensure low-latency path for signed header verification (cache KMS HMAC keys), (2) add clear metrics for 'justification_missing' and 'justification_invalid'.
Author (Priya Raman): Addressed — added an in-memory per-region key cache with TTL and added prometheus metrics justification_missing_total and justification_invalid_total. See commit 2.

Maya Chen: Audit detector is great. Request: include a CSV backfill export with counts per-tenant and sample IDs so compliance team can triage. Also, please add guidance in runbook for rolling the feature on/off.
Author (Priya Raman): Added csv exporter and runbook snippet; included sample Linear task references in docs.
Diego Alvarez: Small nit — ensure the revoker CLI supports dry-run and rate limits (we don't want mass revokes during testing).
Author (Priya Raman): Added --dry-run and --rate-limit flags to epoch-revoker; integration tests include a dry-run scenario.
ci_checks: integration-tests: initially failed (flaky KMS emulator timeout), rerun passed
merge_outcome: Merged via squash by Evan Brooks on 2025-11-19 after green CI and 2 approvals. Release will be included in v2.13.0. The PR body includes a short migration guide; feature default is opt-in. Rolling deployment recommended: enable audit detector in read-only mode for 48h, evaluate blindspot report, then enable enforcement flag and deploy revoker in dry-run prior to active mode.
release_notes: Security: add support for signed operator justification headers (X-Operator-Justification) validated with KMS; audit tool can detect historical blindspots; epoch revoker enforces short-lived elevated RBAC bindings. Opt-in via feature flag security.justification.enforce. See security runbook for rollout steps.
